title: Tailed Long Amplicon Sequencing for AAU-nCoV-2019
author: Emil Aarre Sorensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfc3jiyn
materials: Negative controls of sterile nuclease free water F
Positve control RNA sample G12 and H
DNA quantification Measure the DNA sample concentration using the TECAN instrument with the Qubit 1X dsDNA HS assay kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific) using 1 µL sample.

steps.title: Create journal and metadata
steps.instruction: Create a journal with a unique CJXXX number and record metadata for all samples, including a reference to the sample registration journal and an overview of the samples to be processed.

steps.title: Arrange samples and controls on plate
steps.instruction: Lay out a 96‑well plate as a full plate: include four negative‑control wells (NFW) in C4, F4, C9, F9; one positive‑control RNA in F12; leave G12 and H12 empty for Qubit standards; skip seven samples (C4, F4, C9, F9, F12, G12, H12) for later processing; fill remaining wells with samples. Adjust control positions if plate contains fewer than 80 samples.

steps.title: Clean pre‑PCR laminar flow cabinet
steps.instruction: Before and after use, wipe all items (pipettes, tip boxes, trash bin rack, etc.) with 70 % ethanol, let dry, then wipe again with RNase‑Away. Expose the cabinet to UV light for 15 min. Wipe UV‑sensitive tubes when entering and leaving. Change gloves each entry/exit. Never open production reagents outside the cabinet.

steps.title: Set up consumables for hexamer annealing
steps.instruction: Place on the LAF bench (UV‑treated) for one plate: 1 skirted PCR plate labeled CJXXX_cDNA_pX, 12 cap‑strips (wiped), 1 yellow ice‑block for reagents, 1 96‑well ice‑block, 1 8‑strip PCR tube rack, 1 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, 1 reservoir, and sufficient pipette tips (wiped).

steps.title: Prepare random‑hexamer annealing mastermix
steps.instruction: In the pre‑PCR cabinet, mix the listed reagents in a reservoir, aliquot the mix into the 0.2 mL 96‑well plate stored on the ice‑block, seal with strip‑caps, note batch numbers in the journal, and spin down to collect liquid.

steps.title: Add RNA template and controls
steps.instruction: Clean the pre‑PCR area (70 % ethanol then RNase‑Away) and keep it on ice. Spin down all RNA samples. Transfer 5 µL RNA from each sample well to the corresponding well of the annealing plate (final volume 13 µL). For negative controls add 5 µL nuclease‑free water; for the positive control add 5 µL EXT‑CJ001‑4A. Gently pipette‑mix, seal, and spin down.

steps.title: Anneal hexamers to RNA
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a PCR machine and run the “Random hexamers annealing” program (as provided in /protocols/COVID-19/Corona - Random hexamers annealing.js). After the run, move the plate to ice and incubate ≥1 min.

steps.title: Prepare cDNA synthesis mastermix
steps.instruction: In the pre‑PCR/master‑mix cabinet, assemble the cDNA synthesis mastermix in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube as specified in the Mastermix‑cDNA‑Synthesis‑Mastermix.xlsx, aliquot 7 µL into each well of an 8‑strip PCR‑tube strip (0.2 mL format), seal, place on ice, and record batch numbers.

steps.title: Add cDNA mastermix to annealed samples
steps.instruction: Transfer 7 µL cDNA synthesis mastermix to each well of the annealed‑RNA plate (total volume 20 µL). Gently mix by pipetting, seal, and spin down.

steps.title: Perform cDNA synthesis reaction
steps.instruction: Move the sealed plate to a PCR machine and run the “cDNA synthesis” program (see /protocols/COVID-19/Corona - cDNA synthesis.js).

steps.title: Store cDNA plate
steps.instruction: If the protocol continues the same day, keep the cDNA plate on ice; otherwise store at –18 °C. Label the plate “cDNA_CJXXX_pX” if not already labeled.

steps.title: Prepare primer stock pools
steps.instruction: Resuspend lyophilised primers to 100 µM in sterile water. For each pool, add 10 µL of every primer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, label as “COVID‑19 long‑tailed primer pool1 V3.X” or “pool2 V3.X” with date and CJXXX, and store aliquots. Perform all work in the laminar flow cabinet and QC each new pool before use.

steps.title: Dilute primer stocks to working solution
steps.instruction: If no working solution is available, dilute each 100 µM stock 1:10 in sterile UV‑treated TE buffer or nuclease‑free water to obtain 10 µM working primer pools. Prepare immediately before PCR‑1 mastermix preparation.

steps.title: Clean pre‑PCR cabinet for PCR1
steps.instruction: Clean the pre‑PCR/master‑mix cabinet as in step 3 (70 % ethanol, then RNase‑Away, UV 15 min, glove change, no reagent opening outside).

steps.title: Prepare PCR1 targeting mastermixes
steps.instruction: In the cabinet, prepare two separate PCR1 mastermixes (one per primer pool) according to the Mastermix‑PCR1‑amplification.xlsx. Aliquot each mix into a 0.2 mL tear‑away 96‑well plate (labelled CJXXX_pX_poolX), seal with strip‑caps, note batch numbers, and spin down.

steps.title: Add cDNA to PCR1 mastermixes
steps.instruction: Clean the cDNA work area (70 % ethanol then RNase‑Away). Transfer the two PCR1 mastermix plates to this area, spin down. For each sample, add 2.5 µL cDNA to the corresponding well of each mastermix plate (final volume 25 µL). Perform column‑wise: unseal one column of both plates, pipette 2.5 µL with a multichannel, reseal column. Ensure each sample appears in both pools with matching well IDs. Reseal cDNA plate, store at –18 °C, briefly vortex each PCR plate, and spin down.

steps.title: Run PCR1 amplification
steps.instruction: Program two PCR machines (one per pool) with the “PCR1 amplification” protocol from /protocols/COVID-19/Corona - PCR1 amplficiation.js and run the reactions.

steps.title: Combine PCR1 products from both pools
steps.instruction: Clean the barcoding area (70 % ethanol then RNase‑Away). In a new 96‑well plate, combine the contents of the corresponding wells from PCR1 pool 1 and pool 2 for each biological sample.

steps.title: Clean‑up PCR1 amplicons with SPRI beads
steps.instruction:
Using CleanNGS SPRI beads (1:1 ratio):
1. Vortex bead solution to homogenize.
2. Unseal one column, add 50 µL beads to each well, mix by pipetting up/down; repeat for all columns.
3. Seal with foil, spin briefly, incubate RT 3 min.
4. Place on magnetic rack ~20 s, discard supernatant.
5. Wash beads twice with 190 µL 80 % ethanol, wait 30 s each, discard.
6. Spin, keep on magnet, air‑dry ≤30 s.
7. Resuspend DNA in 18 µL nuclease‑free water, reseal, vortex, spin, incubate RT 2 min, place on magnet until clear.

steps.title: Clean pre‑PCR cabinet for PCR2
steps.instruction: Clean the pre‑PCR/master‑mix cabinet as in step 3 (ethanol, RNase‑Away, UV 15 min, glove change, no reagent opening outside).

steps.title: Prepare PCR2 barcoding mastermix
steps.instruction: In the cabinet, prepare the PCR2 barcoding mastermix per Mastermix‑PCR2‑barcoding‑and‑amplification.xlsx. Aliquot 8 µL of the mix into each well of a 0.2 mL tear‑away 96‑well plate. From the IDT/ILM dual‑index plate, add 2 µL of each barcode primer to the corresponding well (total 10 µL per well). Seal, note barcode IDs, and spin down.

steps.title: Add PCR1 products to barcoding mastermix
steps.instruction: Transfer the PCR1‑combined plate to the barcoding area (magnetic rack present). For each sample, add 15 µL of the bead‑bound PCR1 product to the matching well of the barcoding mastermix plate without disturbing beads. Perform column‑wise: unseal column, add 15 µL, reseal column. Vortex sealed plate, spin down.

steps.title: Run PCR2 barcoding amplification
steps.instruction: Program the PCR machine with the “PCR2 Barcoding Long‑fragment” protocol from /protocols/COVID-19/Corona - PCR2 Barcoding Long-fragment.js and run the reaction.

steps.title: Clean‑up PCR2 amplicons with SPRI beads
steps.instruction:
Using CleanNGS SPRI beads at 0.7:1 ratio (17.5 µL beads per sample):
1. Vortex bead solution.
2. Unseal column, add 17.5 µL beads, mix up/down; repeat for all columns.
3. Seal with foil, spin, incubate RT 3 min.
4. Magnet ~20 s, discard supernatant.
5. Wash twice with 190 µL 80 % ethanol, 30 s each, discard.
6. Spin, air‑dry ≈30 s.
7. Resuspend DNA in 20 µL nuclease‑free water, reseal, vortex, spin, incubate RT 2 min, magnet until clear.

steps.title: Prepare Qubit standards and samples
steps.instruction:
In a 96‑well TECAN plate (full plate):
- Well G12 (Standard 1): 190 µL Qubit 1X dsDNA HS Working Solution + 10 µL Qubit HS Standard #1.
- Well H12 (Standard 2): 190 µL Working Solution + 10 µL Qubit HS Standard #2.
- Remaining wells (samples): 199 µL Working Solution + 1 µL sample.
Seal with foil, vortex 3‑5 s, quick spin, incubate RT 2 min.

steps.title: Measure DNA concentration on TECAN
steps.instruction: Open the TECAN instrument, load the sealed plate, launch the controller software, select the DNA concentration measurement script, assign wells G12 and H12 as standards, start the run. Generate a standard curve from the two standards, calculate sample concentrations, save the Excel file as CJXXX_YYYY‑MM‑DD_PCR2 on /Desktop/EB/Covid19, and enter the concentrations into the journal metadata sheet.

steps.title: Assess DNA integrity on TapeStation
steps.instruction: Prepare ladder in the first tube of a strip: 10 µL D5000 Sample Buffer + 1 µL D5000 Ladder. For each sample: 10 µL Sample Buffer + 1 µL sample. Vortex 2000 rpm 1 min, spin down. Load samples and ladder onto an Agilent 2200 TapeStation (D5000 assay), ensuring the tip‑array is full and no tips are in the trash. Run up to 10 samples with concentrations >1 ng/µL (use D5000 HS assay for lower concentrations). Save the result as CJXXX_YYYY‑MM‑DD_PCR2.

steps.title: Normalize DNA concentrations to 1 ng/µL
steps.instruction: Subtract 0.7 ng/µL from each measured concentration to account for dimer product. For each sample with final concentration ≥1 ng/µL, transfer 5 µL of sample to a new dilution well and add nuclease‑free water to reach 1 ng/µL (volume calculated from the metadata sheet). Skip dilution for samples <1 ng/µL.

steps.title: Pool normalized samples and concentrate
steps.instruction:
For each normalized sample, transfer 3 µL (≈3 ng) to a common pool tube; for negative controls or low‑concentration samples transfer up to 10 µL to obtain ≤3 ng DNA. Store remaining undiluted DNA in a skirted storage plate labeled CJXXX_PCR, seal with foil, and keep at –18 °C.
Concentrate the pooled DNA with CleanNGS SPRI beads at 0.7:1 ratio:
1. Vortex bead solution.
2. Add X µL beads (0.7 × pooled volume) to the pool, flick to mix.
3. Spin briefly, incubate RT 3 min.
4. Magnet ~20 s, discard supernatant.
5. Wash twice with 400 µL 80 % ethanol, 30 s each, discard.
6. Spin, air‑dry ≈30 s.
7. Resuspend in 50 µL nuclease‑free water, vortex, spin, incubate RT 2 min, magnet until clear.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing library for MinION
steps.instruction: Follow the Oxford Nanopore LSK‑SQK‑109 amplicon‑by‑ligation protocol (amplicon‑sqk‑lsk109‑ACDE_9064_v109_revN_14Aug2019‑minion.pdf) using the 50 µL concentrated pool as input. Use 48 µL pooled library, skip the CS DNA step, and retain 1 µL of the library for pre‑ and post‑library‑preparation integrity QC.
